task.goal:
Implement GitHub issue #111: MGA 8/8 — Inspect milestone status and demonstrate a synthetic end-to-end release

Issue body:
> **DRAFT IMPLEMENTATION TICKET — UNAUTHORIZED.** This is a reviewable planning artifact, not permission to run Ralph. Keep it **unlabeled** until the owner explicitly approves the full implementation batch.

## Parent

#103 — Goal-level milestone authorization specification

## What to build

From a fresh ChatGPT conversation or Ralph's existing operator interface, the owner can reliably answer: Which milestone was approved? Which tickets are drafts, authorized, running, waiting, denied or merged? Why was each decision made? A realistic synthetic-only demonstration proves an approved goal can generate and complete dependent work without repeated owner approvals, while an unrelated ready-labeled issue cannot run.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Expose a read-only milestone summary in existing status/result surfaces (or a small operator command), with current grant identity/revision/objective, scope/expiry/quotas, authorized ticket IDs and digests, prerequisites, active jobs and actionable blocked reasons.
- [ ] A restarted ChatGPT conversation can inspect the permanent specification, ticket list, grant revision, receipts, and complete owner-visible job/authorization events without reconstructing earlier chat context.
- [ ] Run a synthetic milestone in an isolated/rehearsal registered project with one allowed issue, a dependent issue and a ready-labeled out-of-scope issue. Demonstrate that the first passes deterministic tests, independent Claude review and exact-SHA CI, merges, then unlocks the second; the out-of-scope ticket never runs.
- [ ] Exercise editing a previously released ticket, grant expiry, pause/revocation during in-flight work, failed batch publication and restart recovery. Verify that stale receipts cannot start or merge jobs and that previous evidence is preserved.
- [ ] Prove R1 and standalone Household admission are not competing schedulers and do not bypass the same grant decision; non-opted-in AgentLoop, Finance Dashboard and Household behavior stays unchanged.
- [ ] Run the full `npm test` suite, independently review code on the exact tested head, verify GitHub CI on that same commit, and report remaining limits and blockers in a durable handoff.
- [ ] Provide a separate, reversible production activation plan (backup, opt-in, health checks and rollback), but **do not** activate a live milestone or deploy from this ticket. Deployment requires later explicit owner authorization.
- [ ] Mark demonstration successful only from verifiable job evidence and product acceptance checks, not merely GitHub issue closure or the presence of a merged PR.

## Blocked by

- #108: Enforce milestone receipts in the Household autopilot
- #109: Release approved ticket batches safely across retries
- #110: Pause, amend or revoke milestones without losing work

Depends on: #108, #109, #110

## Delivery safeguards

No live milestone activation, owner registry edit, service restart, unreviewed execution, new scheduler, or production deployment. Test against isolated durable job stores and fake GitHub, preserve all captured logs, and retain existing exact-head CI/independent review/guarded merge protections. Approval and deployment remain separate decisions.

Repository instructions:
--- AGENTS.md ---
# AgentLoop agent instructions

Before changing AgentLoop/Ralph R1 transcripts, execution logs, project onboarding, CLI/sandbox rules, VM/host access, or deployment, **read** [ADR 0001: Owner visibility and disposable-VM trust boundary](docs/decisions/0001-agentloop-trust-boundary.md). This is an accepted owner policy, not a pending security-review proposal. Implement complete owner-visible captured logs and protect the physical Windows host rather than disposable VM contents.

Follow the linked ADR and the active GitHub issue's acceptance criteria; never treat a merged change as a verified deployment.

For Pocock `to-spec` / `to-tickets` planning, follow the committed [GitHub issue-tracker convention](docs/github-issue-tracker.md). Draft publication creates an unlabeled planning artifact and suppresses ready-label behavior, including retries. Explicit executable release requires separate owner authorization; publishing a draft does not authorize Ralph execution or production configuration changes. Preserve existing instructions, installed skills, and owner settings.

> **DRAFT IMPLEMENTATION TICKET — UNAUTHORIZED.** This is a reviewable planning artifact, not permission to run Ralph. Keep it **unlabeled** until the owner explicitly approves the full implementation batch.

## Parent

#103 — Goal-level milestone authorization specification

## What to build

From a fresh ChatGPT conversation or Ralph's existing operator interface, the owner can reliably answer: Which milestone was approved? Which tickets are drafts, authorized, running, waiting, denied or merged? Why was each decision made? A realistic synthetic-only demonstration proves an approved goal can generate and complete dependent work without repeated owner approvals, while an unrelated ready-labeled issue cannot run.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Expose a read-only milestone summary in existing status/result surfaces (or a small operator command), with current grant identity/revision/objective, scope/expiry/quotas, authorized ticket IDs and digests, prerequisites, active jobs and actionable blocked reasons.
- [ ] A restarted ChatGPT conversation can inspect the permanent specification, ticket list, grant revision, receipts, and complete owner-visible job/authorization events without reconstructing earlier chat context.
- [ ] Run a synthetic milestone in an isolated/rehearsal registered project with one allowed issue, a dependent issue and a ready-labeled out-of-scope issue. Demonstrate that the first passes deterministic tests, independent Claude review and exact-SHA CI, merges, then unlocks the second; the out-of-scope ticket never runs.
- [ ] Exercise editing a previously released ticket, grant expiry, pause/revocation during in-flight work, failed batch publication and restart recovery. Verify that stale receipts cannot start or merge jobs and that previous evidence is preserved.
- [ ] Prove R1 and standalone Household admission are not competing schedulers and do not bypass the same grant decision; non-opted-in AgentLoop, Finance Dashboard and Household behavior stays unchanged.
- [ ] Run the full `npm test` suite, independently review code on the exact tested head, verify GitHub CI on that same commit, and report remaining limits and blockers in a durable handoff.
- [ ] Provide a separate, reversible production activation plan (backup, opt-in, health checks and rollback), but **do not** activate a live milestone or deploy from this ticket. Deployment requires later explicit owner authorization.
- [ ] Mark demonstration successful only from verifiable job evidence and product acceptance checks, not merely GitHub issue closure or the presence of a merged PR.

- #108: Enforce milestone receipts in the Household autopilot
- #109: Release approved ticket batches safely across retries
- #110: Pause, amend or revoke milestones without losing work

Depends on: #108, #109, #110

No live milestone activation, owner registry edit, service restart, unreviewed execution, new scheduler, or production deployment. Test against isolated durable job stores and fake GitHub, preserve all captured logs, and retain existing exact-head CI/independent review/guarded merge protections. Approval and deployment remain separate decisions.

# ADR 0001: Owner visibility and disposable-VM trust boundary

- **Status:** Accepted by the operator, 2026-10-16 (America/New_York)
- **Scope:** Woods-controlled Ralph / AgentLoop autonomous development and project onboarding
- **Decision authority:** Owner-approved operator policy, not a finding of an autonomous security reviewer
- **Issue sequence:** #90 (complete transcripts) -> #84 (Node) -> #85 (Python) -> #86 (registration) -> #87 (migration and host checks)

## Context

Ralph is an operator-controlled agent orchestrator running in a disposable Linux VM. Its agents implement code and operate on VM-local repositories, which may be destroyed and restored. The owner wants autonomy and direct visibility, rather than a multitenant security boundary that hides the system's work from its operator.

Prior R1 transcript changes (#36, #39, PR #89) attempted to prevent information disclosure to the owner by emitting only sanitized, highly compressed lifecycle messages. That design made actual failures difficult to diagnose. Likewise, onboarding #84/#85 introduced mandatory per-project filesystem isolation inside the disposable VM, even when that isolation prevented normal installed tools from being found. These policies protect low-value VM contents at the expense of development and observability.

## Decision

### 1. Protect the physical host, not the disposable VM

**High-value boundary:** the Windows physical host and any host-only files, credentials, private services, or privileges. Verify and constrain paths by which processes in the VM could affect the host. In WSL2 or other VM environments, explicitly check mounts, Windows executable interoperability, forwarded credentials and SSH agents, shared sockets, hypervisor/management interfaces, and network-reachable host services. A VM is not assumed isolated simply because it is called a VM.

**Accepted disposable assets:** the Linux VM installation, VM-local files and credentials, project worktrees, code, local Git history, and repositories the owner explicitly assigns to the agents. Data loss or destructive mistakes in that scope are operational recovery problems, not the primary security boundary. External systems or accounts outside the owner's authorized project scope are not implicitly disposable.

Do not change the Windows host's security settings or disable user-required host integrations without an explicit owner decision. Flag any discovered bridge into high-value host resources with a concrete non-destructive verification and recommended mitigation.

### 2. Owner observability is mandatory

Everything that AgentLoop actually captures about a job must be available **verbatim** to the owner: worker/critic output, stdout and stderr, commands, tool events made available by the engine, verification results, traces, errors, review findings, retry decisions, and orchestration events. Preserve execution records after failures, restarts and worktree cleanup.

Present a readable chronological timeline with access to **complete raw records**. Rendering may escape markup, neutralize terminal controls, page results or offer full-log downloads, but must not hide or irreversibly truncate captured content. A concise summary is navigation, never the only record. Do not redact or suppress captured content to protect the owner from seeing it. The dashboard remains controlled by the operator; who may access it is an access-control issue, not a reason to censor it for the owner.

Only expose what the actual engine makes available. Do not claim to capture or reconstruct model reasoning that the model or CLI does not expose.

### 3. Prefer ordinary in-VM execution and reliable recovery

Use conventional locked builds: Node with committed package-lock.json and npm ci; Python with pyproject.toml, committed uv.lock and uv sync --locked. Use ordinary VM-local commands and system executables. **Do not require an additional bubblewrap/per-worktree command sandbox or secret-canary tests protecting only VM contents**, and do not block work merely because that internal sandbox is unavailable. Optional isolation may be used for a concrete engineering purpose, but is not a hard onboarding gate.

Keep independent implementation review, deterministic tests, exact-commit GitHub CI, bounded retries, process cancellation, durable jobs, staged registration, owner activation decisions and deployment rollback. These controls serve correctness, recoverability and operator intent. They must not become a reason to conceal the associated logs.

Lockfiles are for repeatability. Familiar package managers, routine vulnerability advisories and normal dependency sources suffice; do not add a bespoke network/egress scanner, package approval service, wheel-hash inventory or alternate high-assurance build mode.

### 4. Preserve the existing delivery boundaries

Registration, readiness and activation remain separate operational facts. Failing application tests are work for coding agents, not automatically an infrastructure failure. An issue merge is not a live deployment. Live config changes and host-boundary changes require their own verified, reversible procedures; do not overwrite operator-modified configuration or erase failed R1 job history just to rearm an issue.

## Consequences and implementation order

1. **#90 first:** replace sanitized-only transcripts (including the policy implemented in PR #89) with complete owner-facing execution records. The old implementation may remain until this successor is tested and deployed; the architectural decision is effective now.
2. **#84:** retain common project contract, Node lockfile setup, preflight/readiness separation and deterministic verification; remove the mandatory internal OS filesystem sandbox and its canary/fail-closed tests.
3. **#85:** use the same execution model for Python and uv --locked; remove old wheel inventory and nested isolation requirements.
4. **#86:** implement staged project registration and owner approval for activation, with full setup diagnostics; do not create a new security-permission service.
5. **#87:** migrate Finance and AgentLoop, prove full job logs and recovery, and check the **actual** VM-to-host boundary non-destructively before a separately reviewed deployment.

## Acceptance rule for future changes

If a proposed change hides captured job data from its owner, makes a VM-internal filesystem sandbox or isolation layer a hard gate for project execution, or overlooks an actual path to physical-host exposure, it conflicts with this accepted decision. Correctness, safety of the physical host, operator visibility and recoverability should determine implementation and review criteria.
# GitHub issue tracking for Pocock planning

This repository-local convention applies when a ChatGPT planner uses Pocock
`to-spec` or `to-tickets` workflows. Keep the globally installed skills and owner
settings unchanged. Reuse existing GitHub issue operations and their shared CLI
transport; do not create another tracker, queue, or scheduler.

Draft publication creates an ordinary GitHub issue with **zero labels**, a
`[DRAFT]` title, and an explicit unauthorized notice. GitHub issues do not have
a native draft state: the notice communicates intent and the absence of labels
keeps these issues out of label-based Ralph admission. The notice alone is not
an admission control. Explicit executable release is a separate owner decision
for the entire batch. The draft helper implements no release operation. The separate
[exact-ticket authorization workflow](milestone-grants.md#exact-ticket-authorization)
requires an active owner-approved grant and explicit exact-ticket scope confirmation.
The [conversation-initiated batch workflow](milestone-grants.md#conversation-initiated-batch-release)
adds a durable journal around draft creation, native blockers and separately
approved receipt/label release. Use that workflow for resumable batches; retain
the standalone helper's read-only retry rule below for standalone publication.

## Planner procedure

1. Extract the proposal and testable acceptance criteria from the existing
   planning conversation. Record a durable conversation URL or an owner-readable
   conversation/message reference in `conversation`. Cite the source specification
   as `#N` or its GitHub issue URL in `sourceSpec`. A specification draft may cite
   its parent specification. The planner must check that criteria are verifiable;
   syntax validation cannot determine their quality.
2. Produce JSON using [the blocker-free ticket example](examples/planning-ticket.json).
   `kind` is `spec` or `ticket`; both use the same schema. `id` is a stable,
   repository-scoped lowercase identifier, retained across retries. Required fields
   are `id`, `kind`, `repo`, `title`, `sourceSpec`, `conversation`, `summary`,
   `acceptanceCriteria` (nonempty string array), and `blockers` (integer array).
   Prose fields are nonempty single lines. Optional `labels` must be `[]`.
   Unknown fields, including ready-label settings, are rejected.
3. Generate the complete owner-facing preview locally:

   ```sh
   node src/planning-drafts.js preview docs/examples/planning-ticket.json
   ```

   Review the full output, including every criterion and blocker. The committed
   [full example preview](examples/planning-ticket-preview.md) is generated by
   this command from the owner-supplied #104 planning conversation. No real issue
   was created to generate it.
4. Only when draft publication to the target account is authorized, publish the
   reviewed JSON with the repository helper:

   ```sh
   node src/planning-drafts.js publish path/to/reviewed-draft.json
   ```

   This ticket's implementation/testing authorization excludes real account
   access; use fake GitHub operations for its demonstration. Issue #104 itself
   must remain unlabeled. The examples are not publication instructions for the
   running agent.

**Suppress the normal `to-spec`/`to-tickets` ready-label step completely**, both
on initial publication and on retries. Do not run their usual publication or
post-publication labeling steps. Use their planning output as input to this
repository helper. Do not pass through any labels, including an owner-configured
custom ready label. Do not compensate for failures with `gh issue edit`, add a
label later, enqueue a Ralph job, or modify project registration. The helper
accepts no queue, registration, or release callback. API creation supplies only
title/body, avoiding CLI issue-template label defaults.

## Dependencies and retries

Use [the dependent example](examples/dependent-planning-ticket.json) for blockers.
It renders exactly `Depends on: #104` on its own line. R1 requires one to eight
unique, smaller-numbered same-repository issues. `blockers: []` renders `None.`
and omits the dependency marker entirely. Native GitHub blocking links may be
added separately if available, but never replace R1 metadata. The helper validates
R1 ordering against the allocated issue number; if GitHub returns an unexpected
number, publication is unconfirmed and requires inspection.

The helper lists all issue pages and states to find the stable draft marker
before creating anything. An existing issue must match the complete preview,
be open and unlabeled, and have valid R1 dependencies. Duplicate markers,
changed content, any labels, malformed responses, and closed drafts fail closed.
It never edits, strips labels from, or reopens an existing issue.

A failed or malformed creation response may mean GitHub already created the
issue. Retain the JSON and full error as owner evidence. **Every retry must use
read-only reconciliation**, which never issues another creation request:

```sh
node src/planning-drafts.js retry path/to/reviewed-draft.json
```

If no matching issue is visible, reconciliation fails without writing. The owner
must inspect the ambiguous attempt and confirm that no issue exists before
starting a fresh `publish`; do not blindly rerun `publish` or generate a new ID.
Unexpected labels are an unconfirmed publication requiring owner inspection,
not permission to continue with release. Concurrent initial publishers for the
same ID are unsupported; use one publisher per draft. Server-side automation
that independently labels issues is outside this helper's control and must be
considered by the owner before authorizing publication.

## Delivery and evidence

`node test/planning-drafts.test.js` exercises creation, preview, invalid metadata,
custom and default ready labels, duplicate identity, transport failure, ambiguous
responses, and read-only retries with fake GitHub operations. It verifies the
production `autopilot-projects.json` and `config.json` contents remain unchanged.
`npm test` includes these tests and remains the GitHub CI entry point.

Keep the existing AgentLoop queue, durable execution evidence, independent Claude
review, exact-head-SHA CI, and guarded merge process for delivery. This helper
bypasses none of those controls and changes no production registration or owner
settings. A local test pass is not an independent review, GitHub CI pass, merge,
or verified deployment. Eventual executable release and live rollout each require
their existing separate authorization.

# Owner milestone grants

Grant commands store authorization evidence only. They do not publish issues,
apply labels, enqueue jobs, enable enforcement, change project settings, or start a
daemon. The separate exact-ticket release workflow below can apply a ready label. Admission remains unchanged for projects that have not opted in. Run these commands in the
existing owner operator environment, using the same owner configuration paths and
`AGENTLOOP_STATE_DIR` across restarts. Do not derive activation commands from issue
text or model responses: activation is an explicit owner decision.

Create an input JSON file with exactly these fields:

```json
{
  "project": "ralph",
  "repo": "woodsja/AgentLoop",
  "spec": {
    "identity": "woodsja/AgentLoop#103@owner-approved-revision-1",
    "digest": "<64 lowercase hex characters: SHA-256 of exact specification file bytes>"
  },
  "objective": "Implement the eight approved milestone tickets",
  "allowedCategories": ["implementation", "tests", "documentation"],
  "exclusions": ["production deployment", "owner configuration changes"],
  "revision": 1,
  "ticketLimit": 8,
  "expiresAt": "2026-11-01T00:00:00.000Z",
  "concurrencyLimit": 2
}
```

The project name and exact repository spelling must match a unique registration
in both owner configuration files, including the same canonical checkout. Staged
and active registered projects are eligible. Wildcards and unrestricted category
names are rejected. Category names use lowercase letters, digits and hyphens.
Ticket limits are integers from 1 to 100; concurrency is 1 to 10 and cannot exceed
the ticket limit. Expiration must be a canonical UTC ISO timestamp in the future,
within 366 days. These conservative initial bounds are not scheduler settings.

```sh
ralph grant draft milestone-1 --input grant.json --spec approved-spec.md --config /owner/config.json --projects /owner/projects.json
ralph grant inspect milestone-1 --config /owner/config.json --projects /owner/projects.json
ralph grant activate milestone-1 --digest <digest-from-inspect> --config /owner/config.json --projects /owner/projects.json
```

Activation previews the complete stored grant and prompts in a terminal. An owner
may instead supply `--yes` together with the inspected digest. Specification
identity, digest and exact bytes are retained in the draft; approval covers those
bytes and all grant terms. Changing the source file later cannot change the grant.
The grant digest is SHA-256 over the fixed-order stored terms, including registration
identity and specification bytes. Actor names come from the local operator account.
Revisions are positive integers; changed terms require a new grant ID and approval.
Repeating a draft with identical terms or activating an already active grant with
the matching digest returns the existing result without duplicating authorization.

`inspect` includes all lifecycle timestamps and approval events, including approval
requests and failures. The existing owner diagnostics log also captures complete
command previews, results and errors. The store is
`$AGENTLOOP_STATE_DIR/milestone-grants.json` (default: repository `state/`). Lifecycle
states are `draft`, `active`, `expired`, `paused`, `revoked`, and `completed`.
Inspection/activation persist expiration of draft, active and paused grants;
revoked and completed remain terminal. Pause, revoke and complete commands belong
to ticket 7 and are deliberately unavailable here.

Grant state and approval events are committed together by fsynced temporary-file
replacement and directory fsync. Interrupted approvals never resume automatically.
A crash before publication leaves the prior state; a crash after publication may
leave a fully approved active grant, which an explicit retry can inspect. Writers
share existing project registration locks, preventing concurrent registration or
grant edits. External owner edits are rechecked after approval. As with project
registration, a killed process can leave `.project-lock` directories next to the
configuration files and grant store. Inspect their `owner.json` records and verify
the owning process is stopped before removing those lock directories and retrying.
Unpublished `.tmp` files are never loaded. Preserve failed diagnostics; do not
replace or reset the grant store to recover a lock.

This change is implementation only. Independent review, exact-SHA CI and guarded
merge remain delivery requirements; none establishes a verified deployment.

## Exact-ticket authorization

This staged implementation adds explicit `ticket preview`, `ticket approve` and
`ticket release` commands. These commands do **not** enable milestone enforcement, modify live
configuration, enqueue a job, or authorize deployment. R1 enforcement is available
only through the separately owner-configured opt-in described below. Household
uses that same opt-in and validator through its existing autopilot.
Do not run release against live projects until those admission protections are
implemented and rollout is separately authorized. All implementation tests use
fake GitHub operations and isolated registrations.

A planner supplies a request JSON with exactly these fields:

```json
{
  "repo": "owner/demo",
  "issue": 106,
  "grantDigest": "<inspected grant SHA-256>",
  "revision": 1,
  "spec": {
    "identity": "owner/demo#103@owner-approved-revision-1",
    "digest": "<approved specification SHA-256>"
  },
  "ticketDigest": "<SHA-256 of JSON.stringify([exactTitle, exactBody]) in UTF-8>",
  "category": "tests",
  "scope": "in-scope",
  "reason": "Adds isolated tests within the approved objective; no excluded changes."
}
```

`scope` is `in-scope`, `ambiguous`, or `excluded`. These are planner declarations,
never authorization. Because category names and prose exclusions do not provide
machine-verifiable semantic permission, the conservative initial evaluator
requires owner confirmation of every exact ticket's scope. An LLM's verdict has
no authorization role. The owner must inspect the **entire title/body**, objective,
approved specification bytes, category and every exclusion in the preview. Owner
confirmation attests that the ticket fits the existing grant; it cannot enlarge
that grant. An excluded category or proposal is denied. An ambiguous request
remains held: resolve it with the owner and submit a precise in-scope request,
or obtain a new grant with separately approved terms. Do not merely relabel
excluded work as a permitted category.

In an isolated operator environment:

```sh
ralph ticket preview milestone-1 --input request.json --config /owner/config.json --projects /owner/projects.json
ralph ticket approve milestone-1 --input request.json --digest <request-digest-from-preview> --config /owner/config.json --projects /owner/projects.json
ralph ticket release milestone-1 --input request.json --config /owner/config.json --projects /owner/projects.json
```

Only the owner runs `approve`, using a terminal prompt or explicit `--yes` with
the inspected request digest. Planner requests must never invoke this owner-only
step automatically. Approval records exact scope but does not consume quota or
write a label. `release` independently checks the grant and GitHub issue again.
The request digest covers grant ID, all request fields and the configured ready
label. Editing the reason, category, label, issue, title/body, specification or
grant revision invalidates the prior confirmation. Grant terms and retained
specification bytes are hash-checked against owner-approved evidence.

Every decision returns `decision` (`ALLOW`, `WAIT`, `NEEDS_APPROVAL`, `DENY`),
human-readable `reasons`, the request digest, full issue, category, grant and
blockers. `WAIT` indicates missing, malformed or unconfirmed GitHub evidence;
`NEEDS_APPROVAL` indicates missing owner scope confirmation or ambiguity; `DENY`
indicates mismatched authorization, excluded scope, inactive/expired grants or
exhausted quota. An unknown/corrupt store or failed durable write raises an error
and writes no executable label. CLI diagnostics retain the full error. Preview
performs no GitHub mutations, but persists its decision for owner inspection.
Blockers use existing R1 dependency syntax and are displayed; satisfying them
remains the existing admission system's responsibility.

The shared grant store retains `ticketApprovals`, `receipts` and `ticketEvents`.
Receipts bind the exact repository/issue, request, title/body digest and bytes,
grant ID/digest/revision, timestamp and unique receipt ID. The full receipt and
one quota reservation are committed atomically **before** the configured label
is written. All grant/registration writers share the same locks; unexpected
external store edits fail rather than being overwritten. Receipts are immutable:
a changed request for a receipted issue is rejected. Retrying the identical
request reuses its receipt, including after failed or ambiguous labeling. If
GitHub already shows the receipted ready label, retry performs no label write.
No labels other than the configured ready label are accepted on a retry.

Decision events retain full ticket content, blockers, grant references, digest,
category and reasons, including before authorization and after release. Existing
owner diagnostics retain complete command output and errors. Receipt quota
counts distinct issues, including unconfirmed label attempts, never retries.
Preserve receipts and logs when reconciling failures; do not reset the store.

GitHub does not provide an atomic compare-title/body-and-add-label operation.
This helper reads the issue again immediately before receipt creation and label
mutation, but a concurrent edit can still race the label write. Receipts never
confer authority on changed bytes: receipt validation in **both** R1 and Household
admission is required before live rollout. The opt-in below provides admission protection in both runners; live rollout
requires a separate owner decision.

`node test/milestone-tickets.test.js` exercises the isolated grant/draft/approval/
receipt/mock-label flow, failures, retries, quota, exact identity and scope holds.
It is included in `npm test` for exact-head CI and the existing independent review
and guarded merge pipeline.


## Conversation-initiated batch release

`ralph batch preview|publish|approve|release GRANT --input batch.json` composes
the existing planning drafts and exact-ticket receipts. These are explicit
commands initiated from a ChatGPT planning conversation, with no scheduler,
background generator, admission bypass, production settings change or deployment.
The input has exactly `id`, `conversation` and `tickets`:

```json
{
  "id": "tests-batch-1",
  "conversation": "chatgpt:owner-planning-message-1",
  "tickets": [
    {
      "draft": {
        "id": "isolated-grant-tests",
        "kind": "ticket",
        "repo": "owner/demo",
        "title": "Add isolated grant tests",
        "sourceSpec": "#103",
        "conversation": "chatgpt:owner-planning-message-1",
        "summary": "Exercise approved grant behavior in temporary stores",
        "acceptanceCriteria": ["The isolated tests pass"],
        "blockers": []
      },
      "category": "tests",
      "scope": "in-scope",
      "reason": "Only approved test scope; no deployment or external permissions."
    }
  ]
}
```

Each `draft` uses the existing planning schema, has kind `ticket`, a distinct
stable ID, and the same explicit conversation reference as the batch. Its source
specification must identify the grant's approved issue (the specification identity
must contain `#N`, optionally followed by `@revision`). Unknown specifications,
cross-repository references and conflicting native blockers require owner review.
The category and scope claims never prove semantic permission. Every exact
title/body, including any newly required external permission, still needs the
existing explicit owner scope confirmation against the objective, specification
and exclusions. Editing authorized bytes immediately invalidates admission.

In the isolated operator environment, using the same `--config`, `--projects`
and `AGENTLOOP_STATE_DIR` as the grant:

```sh
ralph batch preview milestone-1 --input batch.json
ralph batch publish milestone-1 --input batch.json
ralph batch preview milestone-1 --input batch.json
ralph batch approve milestone-1 --input batch.json --digest <batch-preview-digest>
ralph batch preview milestone-1 --input batch.json
ralph batch release milestone-1 --input batch.json
```

`publish` is separately authorized draft publication: it creates unlabeled issues
and reconciles native blocking links to the exact body `Depends on:` metadata.
It never approves scope or applies readiness labels. `approve` is owner-only,
requires the inspected complete batch digest (including the grant digest), and prompts separately for each
exact ticket. `release` cannot invoke approval. Repeating these commands retains
the immutable batch and issue identities. Unknown extra fields are rejected.

Preview performs no GitHub writes and shows every draft, allocated issue identity,
dependencies, grant evidence, receipt, decision and explanation. Before publication,
an unresolved remote identity is `WAIT`. Published unapproved tickets are
`NEEDS_APPROVAL`; invalid grants and exhausted issued quota are `DENY`. Approved
tickets awaiting independently reviewed, exact-head green CI and merged durable
Ralph prerequisite evidence are `WAIT`. Neither a closed GitHub issue nor a
ticket elsewhere in the batch satisfies a prerequisite. The existing project job
store is read using its registered `stateDir`, or the project directory beneath
the owner state root. These checks do not create jobs or alter prerequisite proof.

`usage` reports issued reservations and the grant's total and active limits;
preview also reports current active usage and projects capacity in input order.
An active reservation means an open receipted GitHub issue, including an
unconfirmed label write. A closed issue frees active capacity, never issued
capacity and never dependency proof. Unavailable identity/state evidence holds
release. `WAIT` tickets without receipts consume no capacity. All receipt writers
share grant/registration locks, so racing attempts fail closed rather than
oversubscribing either quota. Retried receipts consume no additional capacity.

The fsynced `milestone-batches.json` journal uses the batch ID plus immutable input
digest, planning marker, GitHub number and blocker write intents as deduplication
keys. All batch publishers using this owner state share one journal lock.
Creation intent is durable before the issue POST. After any ambiguous attempt,
retry only reconciles the stable marker across all issue pages/states; it never
repeats creation. If no issue is visible, owner inspection is required. Likewise,
an uncertain native-blocker POST is reconciled by a fresh read; absence holds for
owner inspection instead of blindly repeating the write. Body dependencies are
supplied in the original immutable creation payload. Native/body discrepancies
cannot authorize a receipt. Each receipt and quota reservation is committed
before its readiness label, and successful-but-unacknowledged labels reconcile
without another mutation. A partial batch retains every prior receipt and event.

Both runners recheck native blocker sets for batch receipts at existing admission
and merge gates, so later native edits invalidate authorization even if the body
did not change. Changed title/body or scope needs reassessment with a new batch
identity; original receipts are retained and cannot be overwritten. A different
grant cannot issue another receipt for an already receipted issue: reconcile with
the owner. The batch command does not implement automatic receipt replacement or upgrade a
legacy receipt that lacks native blocker evidence.

GitHub has no distributed transaction spanning issue creation, native links,
local fsynced state and labels. This protocol preserves uncertain intents rather
than claiming a failed remote request did nothing. Full issues, requests, errors
and decisions remain owner-visible in the existing execution diagnostics, ticket
events and batch journal. A killed process may leave the existing `.project-lock`
directories; inspect `owner.json`, verify the process stopped, then remove only
the abandoned locks before retrying. Never reset either journal or grant receipts.
Do not concurrently use the standalone draft publisher for the same identities;
it does not participate in the batch lock.

writes, creation/native/label response loss, abrupt process exits after creation,
native linking, receipt commit and labeling, edits, dependency holds, active/issued quota and
concurrent publishers with fake GitHub and temporary durable stores. It runs in
`npm test`. These implementation tests authorize no live release or deployment.

## R1 milestone admission (disabled on live projects)

The optional boolean `milestoneAuthorization` in an existing registered R1
project's autopilot policy enables receipt enforcement when it is exactly `true`.
Omission or `false` preserves existing R1 admission, review, labels and automatic
merge behavior. No shipped project enables it. Enabling a live project requires a
separate owner rollout decision; this implementation does not authorize that edit.

The existing R1 queue calls one read-only validator during periodic discovery,
direct/manual submission, queue advancement and resumed execution. Reserved mixed
implementation children are checked again before starting. The same validator
checks continuation before integration, worker admission, delivery and independent
review, and immediately before the guarded merge request. It reads the current
GitHub issue and the durable grant store again; cached labels and a prior receipt
check cannot authorize a later merge. Existing tests, independent Claude review,
exact-head CI, PR identity and target integration gates remain required.

Admission requires one exact receipt, active unexpired owner-approved grant,
unchanged grant/specification bytes and registered identity, exact scope approval,
and unchanged issue title/body at the exact repository/number with its configured
ready label. Queued tasks retain the exact grant/receipt binding, so an in-flight
job cannot silently switch to a replacement receipt. Dependency proof still requires independently reviewed, exact-head
CI-green merged job evidence; a closed issue is insufficient. GitHub reads or
store/configuration reads that fail or change during the check deny execution.
GitHub and the local store cannot participate in a single transaction: a change
after the final read cannot be atomically coupled to GitHub's merge operation.

The validator uses the same owner configuration, projects file and global
`AGENTLOOP_STATE_DIR/milestone-grants.json` as the grant/ticket commands, rather
than a worker-provided path or the per-project job store. Embedders can supply
`projectsPath` to `createR1Jobs` when using an isolated owner projects file.
Denied checks append and fsync specific diagnostics to
`$AGENTLOOP_STATE_DIR/milestone-admission.ndjson`. Existing task execution records
also retain execution/merge authorization failures. Authorization holds preserve
worktrees, branches, labels, attempts, reviews and captured output for owner
reconciliation; automatic cleanup does not remove held work.

`node test/r1-milestone-admission.test.js` uses isolated owner policies, the actual
R1 submit/discover/recover/advance/merge paths, fake GitHub and the real grant and
receipt commands. It covers missing/corrupt/unreadable authorization, dependency
proof and revocation, expiry or issue edits after green CI and independent PASS.


## Household milestone admission (disabled on live projects)

A registered project with `dependencyFormat: "household-blocked-by"` retains
its existing Household autopilot and `## Blocked by` parsing. Setting
`milestoneAuthorization` to exactly `true` additionally selects the shared R1
receipt validator. No shipped owner policy is changed. R1 discovery continues to
skip these projects, so the two runners do not compete for the ready label.

Household selection, including `--dry-run`, checks current receipts and GitHub
identity/content before choosing work. The selected title/body must match the
receipted revision as well as the fresh GitHub read. The issue lock protects new
job creation and recovery; authorization is rechecked under that lock and before
worker admission, integration, delivery, independent review and guarded merge.
Jobs retain their grant/receipt binding across restarts. A prior ready label,
merged prerequisites or a cached receipt never replaces a fresh check.

The shared validator selects Household dependency parsing from registered policy.
Every blocker still needs a terminal merged job with independent exact-head
Claude PASS, green CI, passing verification and reconciled issue closure. These
prerequisites are checked again during continuation and merge. Missing or
malformed metadata cannot silently become a dependency-free ticket.

Selection reports `ALLOW`, `WAIT` (dependency evidence or metadata),
`NEEDS_APPROVAL` (missing receipt or owner scope approval), or `DENY` (invalid,
modified, ambiguous duplicate or expired authorization). All blocking decisions
append fsynced diagnostics to `milestone-admission.ndjson`; no label is removed.
An execution-time hold also retains job evidence and its workspace for owner
reconciliation instead of retrying as a transient worker error. A dry run writes
only local diagnostics; it does not create jobs, mutate grants, execute workers
or write GitHub.

## Pause, resume, amend and retire existing grants

Use the existing owner CLI with the same state/configuration paths as both runners.
Each lifecycle command first prints a complete preview and action digest:

```sh
ralph grant pause milestone-1
ralph grant pause milestone-1 --digest <action-preview-digest>
ralph grant resume milestone-1
ralph grant resume milestone-1 --digest <action-preview-digest>
ralph grant amend milestone-1 --input revision-2.json --spec approved-spec.md
ralph grant amend milestone-1 --input revision-2.json --spec approved-spec.md --digest <action-preview-digest>
```

`revoke`, `expire` and `complete` use the same preview/confirm workflow. Confirmation
prompts the owner; `--yes` supplies explicit noninteractive confirmation. A grant's
term digest used for activation differs from an action digest, which also binds
the action, lifecycle version, current state and proposed amendment. Successful
retries with the same action digest have no effect. Each new pause/resume cycle
has a new digest. Shared owner locks serialize transitions, ticket release and
amendments; out-of-lock edits fail closed. Requests, failures and confirmed actions
remain in the durable event history. Revoked, expired and completed grants cannot
resume. Explicit expiry can retire a grant before its scheduled expiration.

An amendment requires the next integer revision, the complete bounded proposal,
and the exact approved specification bytes. It cannot change the project,
repository or registration identity, or reduce total quota below issued tickets.
The preceding approved revision is retained in `history`. Existing receipts stay
unchanged and cannot authorize the new revision. For an affected ticket, submit a
new exact-ticket request, explicitly approve its semantic scope, then release it.
The old receipt moves to `receiptHistory` when its replacement is durably issued;
the same issue still consumes one issued quota unit. Retained jobs can bind to
that explicitly reapproved replacement, with their earlier binding kept in job
history. Pause/resume alone never upgrades an invalid receipt. Batch journals
continue to bind their original revision and require separate owner reconciliation.

`inspect` prints issued count, remaining total quota, each receipted issue's local
work state and authorization block reasons alongside the full grant and audit
records. A pause or retirement denies new receipt releases, attempts and guarded
merges. Authorization holds retain queue/checkpoint state, worktrees, branches,
CI, independent reviews and raw execution records. Resume rechecks current issue
content, receipt revision, prerequisites and every existing exact-head gate.
Completed merges remain completed.

While an implementation or integration service runs, both runners poll canonical
local grant/receipt state for cooperative cancellation. The native CLI service
requests SIGTERM and waits for actual process closure; mixed R1 children use the
owning daemon cancellation lifecycle. Services without cancellation support record
that limitation and finish under the existing timeout. Cancellation requests,
errors and actual returned results are appended to the execution journal. A
request never proves the process stopped, erases evidence or authorizes delivery.
The native task service checks full admission again before each new attempt.
The daemon also rereads canonical grant/receipt status before every mixed child
worker or critic process, including later cycles.

Expiration uses system time with a fsynced append-only high-water record in
`milestone-clock.ndjson`. Observing expiry in a runner cannot be undone by a later
backward clock transition or process restart. A forward clock jump may expire
authority early; reconcile the clock with the owner instead of deleting evidence
or automatically renewing a grant. Missing, malformed or unreadable authority
fails closed. GitHub merges remain subject to the documented distributed
transaction limitation after the final canonical read.

These commands change only grant evidence. They do not edit owner registries,
credentials, issue specifications, service configuration or deployment state.
Implementation verification uses temporary stores and fake GitHub; no live
activation, service restart or deployment is implied.

test('owner summary is read-only, retains raw evidence and diagnoses damaged stores and expiry', async t => {
  const f = await fixture(t);
  await f.run('publish'); await f.approve(); await f.run('release');
  const { milestoneSummary } = require('../src/milestone-summary');
  const { parseArguments, main } = require('../src/cli');
  assert.equal(parseArguments(['grant', 'summary', 'g1']).action, 'summary');
  assert.throws(() => parseArguments(['grant', 'summary', 'g1', '--yes']), /not valid/);
  const file = path.join(f.root, 'milestone-grants.json');
  const db = f.db(); db.grants.g1.expiresAt = '2000-01-01T00:00:00.000Z';
  fs.writeFileSync(file, JSON.stringify(db));
  fs.mkdirSync(path.join(f.root, 'demo'), { recursive: true });
  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(f.root, 'demo', 'issue-200.json'), '{broken');
  const raw = 'complete raw stdout\\u001b[31m\\n' + 'long evidence '.repeat(10000);
  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(f.root, 'demo', 'issue-200.execution.ndjson'), raw);
  const snapshot = () => {
    const all = {};
    function visit(dir) { for (const entry of fs.readdirSync(dir, { withFileTypes: true })) {
      const name = path.join(dir, entry.name); if (entry.isDirectory()) visit(name); else all[name] = fs.readFileSync(name).toString('base64');
    } }
    visit(f.root); return all;
  };
  const before = snapshot();
  const summary = milestoneSummary('g1', f.options);
  assert.equal(summary.effectiveState, 'expired');
  assert.equal(summary.grant.state, 'active', 'summary does not persist lifecycle changes');
  assert.ok(summary.errors.some(e => e.file?.endsWith('issue-200.json')));
  assert.equal(summary.evidence.find(e => e.file.endsWith('issue-200.execution.ndjson')).raw, raw);
  assert.ok(summary.tickets.every(ticket => ticket.status === 'denied'));
  assert.deepEqual(snapshot(), before);
  // Exercise the real CLI path without importing/initializing the writable owner store.
  const previous = process.env.AGENTLOOP_STATE_DIR, output = console.log;
  process.env.AGENTLOOP_STATE_DIR = f.root; console.log = () => {};
  try {
    const result = await main(['grant', 'summary', 'g1', '--projects', f.options.projectsPath]);
    assert.equal(result.grant.id, 'g1'); assert.deepEqual(snapshot(), before);
  } finally { console.log = output; if (previous === undefined) delete process.env.AGENTLOOP_STATE_DIR; else process.env.AGENTLOOP_STATE_DIR = previous; }
});

## Read-only owner milestone summary

"'```sh
AGENTLOOP_STATE_DIR=/owner/state node src/cli.js grant summary milestone-1 --projects /owner/projects.json
```

Use the same state directory and registry as the operator. `summary` reads files
without initializing the writable CLI store, taking locks, advancing the durable
clock, persisting expiry, calling GitHub, or starting work. Standard output is a
single JSON report suitable for saving and inspecting in a fresh conversation.
Unlike `inspect`, it never persists lifecycle transitions. It accepts no approval
flags. Missing/corrupt evidence is reported in `errors`; the raw bytes remain in
`evidence`. An unknown grant or unreadable grant store fails inspection.

The report includes current grant identity, revision, digest, objective, retained
specification bytes (`spec.contentBase64`), scope, expiry, quotas, exact authorized
ticket IDs/digests, planned drafts, batch journals, dependencies, jobs, recorded
decisions/reasons, admission diagnostics and full captured execution journals.
`lastDecision` and `lastAdmission` are historical evidence, not fresh GitHub
observations. A merged status describes retained job evidence; it is not product
acceptance or deployment verification. Receipts and approval history remain
available in full even when the grant is paused, amended, revoked or expired.

This is a local, non-atomic snapshot while writers may run. Repeat inspection
when evidence changes. It cannot detect a remote edit made since the last job or
release observation; existing admission and guarded merge must reread GitHub.
`authorized` describes a stored receipt, never permission to skip those gates.
Issued quota includes every retained reservation; active job count describes local
jobs and differs from release'"'s open-issue capacity calculation. The report embeds
complete raw records without truncation, including operator diagnostics across
grants in this owner state root. Large histories produce large reports. Keep the
report in the existing owner access boundary and preserve source stores/logs.

For reproducible rehearsal coverage, evidence limits, and the separately gated
activation procedure, see [issue 111 handoff](issue-111-handoff.md).

test('an unexplained push response is reconciled read-only and never authorizes a blind retry', async t => {

    const f = await fixture(t), clock = { time: Date.now() };
    let pushes = 0;
    const tick = retryRunner(f, transportAdapter(args => args[0] === 'push', (file, args, opts, cb, native) => {
      pushes++;
      const lost = () => cb(Object.assign(new Error('response unavailable'), { code: 128 }), '', '');

      lost();

    }

});

findings.summary:
1) The durable handoff points to evidence files that are not in this PR. docs/issue-111-handoff.md links evidence/issue-111/npm-test-sandbox.log, evidence/issue-111/npm-test.log (the 723-test full run) and evidence/issue-111/batch-tests.log (the 15 test results). The diff adds only implementation.sha256, rehearsal-acceptance.json and rehearsal.json.gz under docs/evidence/issue-111/. These three logs are the only retained record of the full-suite and sandbox-failure results the handoff cites, so the links are dead and the report of remaining limits is unverifiable. Commit the three logs, or remove the claims and links and state where the output is kept. The retained output must be complete and unmodified, per ADR 0001.

2) The handoff's delivery status is stale for the delivered head. It says the implementation 'remains a working-tree change', that the exact-head review and remote CI are still outstanding, and that gh auth is invalid so CI verification is blocked. The PR head 9661ba4 is committed and has a green CI run (#39893058022). Update the handoff to name the delivered SHA and its CI run. Say plainly that independent review is still performed by the guarded pipeline rather than by the local failed Claude attempts. Also state that implementation.sha256 was computed over the tested contents and re-check that it still matches src/milestone-summary.js, src/cli.js and test/milestone-batches.test.js at this head.

Issue body:
> **DRAFT IMPLEMENTATION TICKET — UNAUTHORIZED.** This is a reviewable planning artifact, not permission to run Ralph. Keep it **unlabeled** until the owner explicitly approves the full implementation batch.

## Parent

#103 — Goal-level milestone authorization specification

## What to build

From a fresh ChatGPT conversation or Ralph's existing operator interface, the owner can reliably answer: Which milestone was approved? Which tickets are drafts, authorized, running, waiting, denied or merged? Why was each decision made? A realistic synthetic-only demonstration proves an approved goal can generate and complete dependent work without repeated owner approvals, while an unrelated ready-labeled issue cannot run.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Expose a read-only milestone summary in existing status/result surfaces (or a small operator command), with current grant identity/revision/objective, scope/expiry/quotas, authorized ticket IDs and digests, prerequisites, active jobs and actionable blocked reasons.
- [ ] A restarted ChatGPT conversation can inspect the permanent specification, ticket list, grant revision, receipts, and complete owner-visible job/authorization events without reconstructing earlier chat context.
- [ ] Run a synthetic milestone in an isolated/rehearsal registered project with one allowed issue, a dependent issue and a ready-labeled out-of-scope issue. Demonstrate that the first passes deterministic tests, independent Claude review and exact-SHA CI, merges, then unlocks the second; the out-of-scope ticket never runs.
- [ ] Exercise editing a previously released ticket, grant expiry, pause/revocation during in-flight work, failed batch publication and restart recovery. Verify that stale receipts cannot start or merge jobs and that previous evidence is preserved.
- [ ] Prove R1 and standalone Household admission are not competing schedulers and do not bypass the same grant decision; non-opted-in AgentLoop, Finance Dashboard and Household behavior stays unchanged.
- [ ] Run the full `npm test` suite, independently review code on the exact tested head, verify GitHub CI on that same commit, and report remaining limits and blockers in a durable handoff.
- [ ] Provide a separate, reversible production activation plan (backup, opt-in, health checks and rollback), but **do not** activate a live milestone or deploy from this ticket. Deployment requires later explicit owner authorization.
- [ ] Mark demonstration successful only from verifiable job evidence and product acceptance checks, not merely GitHub issue closure or the presence of a merged PR.

## Blocked by

- #108: Enforce milestone receipts in the Household autopilot
- #109: Release approved ticket batches safely across retries
- #110: Pause, amend or revoke milestones without losing work

Depends on: #108, #109, #110

## Delivery safeguards

No live milestone activation, owner registry edit, service restart, unreviewed execution, new scheduler, or production deployment. Test against isolated durable job stores and fake GitHub, preserve all captured logs, and retain existing exact-head CI/independent review/guarded merge protections. Approval and deployment remain separate decisions.

This is an accepted owner policy, not a pending security-review proposal. Implement complete owner-visible captured logs and protect the physical Windows host rather than disposable VM contents.

Draft publication creates an unlabeled planning artifact and suppresses ready-label behavior, including retries. Explicit executable release requires separate owner authorization; publishing a draft does not authorize Ralph execution or production configuration changes. # ADR 0001: Owner visibility and disposable-VM trust boundary

- **Status:** Accepted by the operator, 2026-10-16 (America/New_York)
- **Scope:** Woods-controlled Ralph / AgentLoop autonomous development and project onboarding
- **Decision authority:** Owner-approved operator policy, not a finding of an autonomous security reviewer
- **Issue sequence:** #90 (complete transcripts) -> #84 (Node) -> #85 (Python) -> #86 (registration) -> #87 (migration and host checks)

## Context

Ralph is an operator-controlled agent orchestrator running in a disposable Linux VM. Its agents implement code and operate on VM-local repositories, which may be destroyed and restored. The owner wants autonomy and direct visibility, rather than a multitenant security boundary that hides the system's work from its operator.

Prior R1 transcript changes (#36, #39, PR #89) attempted to prevent information disclosure to the owner by emitting only sanitized, highly compressed lifecycle messages. That design made actual failures difficult to diagnose. Likewise, onboarding #84/#85 introduced mandatory per-project filesystem isolation inside the disposable VM, even when that isolation prevented normal installed tools from being found. These policies protect low-value VM contents at the expense of development and observability.

## Decision

### 1. Protect the physical host, not the disposable VM

**High-value boundary:** the Windows physical host and any host-only files, credentials, private services, or privileges. Verify and constrain paths by which processes in the VM could affect the host. In WSL2 or other VM environments, explicitly check mounts, Windows executable interoperability, forwarded credentials and SSH agents, shared sockets, hypervisor/management interfaces, and network-reachable host services. A VM is not assumed isolated simply because it is called a VM.

**Accepted disposable assets:** the Linux VM installation, VM-local files and credentials, project worktrees, code, local Git history, and repositories the owner explicitly assigns to the agents. Data loss or destructive mistakes in that scope are operational recovery problems, not the primary security boundary. External systems or accounts outside the owner's authorized project scope are not implicitly disposable.

Do not change the Windows host's security settings or disable user-required host integrations without an explicit owner decision. Flag any discovered bridge into high-value host resources with a concrete non-destructive verification and recommended mitigation.

### 2. Owner observability is mandatory

Everything that AgentLoop actually captures about a job must be available **verbatim** to the owner: worker/critic output, stdout and stderr, commands, tool events made available by the engine, verification results, traces, errors, review findings, retry decisions, and orchestration events. Preserve execution records after failures, restarts and worktree cleanup.

Present a readable chronological timeline with access to **complete raw records**. Rendering may escape markup, neutralize terminal controls, page results or offer full-log downloads, but must not hide or irreversibly truncate captured content. A concise summary is navigation, never the only record. Do not redact or suppress captured content to protect the owner from seeing it. The dashboard remains controlled by the operator; who may access it is an access-control issue, not a reason to censor it for the owner.

Only expose what the actual engine makes available. Do not claim to capture or reconstruct model reasoning that the model or CLI does not expose.

### 3. Prefer ordinary in-VM execution and reliable recovery

Use conventional locked builds: Node with committed package-lock.json and npm ci; Python with pyproject.toml, committed uv.lock and uv sync --locked. Use ordinary VM-local commands and system executables. **Do not require an additional bubblewrap/per-worktree command sandbox or secret-canary tests protecting only VM contents**, and do not block work merely because that internal sandbox is unavailable. Optional isolation may be used for a concrete engineering purpose, but is not a hard onboarding gate.

Keep independent implementation review, deterministic tests, exact-commit GitHub CI, bounded retries, process cancellation, durable jobs, staged registration, owner activation decisions and deployment rollback. These controls serve correctness, recoverability and operator intent. They must not become a reason to conceal the associated logs.

Lockfiles are for repeatability. Familiar package managers, routine vulnerability advisories and normal dependency sources suffice; do not add a bespoke network/egress scanner, package approval service, wheel-hash inventory or alternate high-assurance build mode.

### 4. Preserve the existing delivery boundaries

Registration, readiness and activation remain separate operational facts. Failing application tests are work for coding agents, not automatically an infrastructure failure. An issue merge is not a live deployment. Live config changes and host-boundary changes require their own verified, reversible procedures; do not overwrite operator-modified configuration or erase failed R1 job history just to rearm an issue.

## Consequences and implementation order

1. **#90 first:** replace sanitized-only transcripts (including the policy implemented in PR #89) with complete owner-facing execution records. The old implementation may remain until this successor is tested and deployed; the architectural decision is effective now.
2. **#84:** retain common project contract, Node lockfile setup, preflight/readiness separation and deterministic verification; remove the mandatory internal OS filesystem sandbox and its canary/fail-closed tests.
3. **#85:** use the same execution model for Python and uv --locked; remove old wheel inventory and nested isolation requirements.
4. **#86:** implement staged project registration and owner approval for activation, with full setup diagnostics; do not create a new security-permission service.
5. **#87:** migrate Finance and AgentLoop, prove full job logs and recovery, and check the **actual** VM-to-host boundary non-destructively before a separately reviewed deployment.

## Acceptance rule for future changes

If a proposed change hides captured job data from its owner, makes a VM-internal filesystem sandbox or isolation layer a hard gate for project execution, or overlooks an actual path to physical-host exposure, it conflicts with this accepted decision. Correctness, safety of the physical host, operator visibility and recoverability should determine implementation and review criteria.

const path = require('node:path');

const { dependencies, eligibleIssues } = require('./r1-dependencies');

function milestoneSummary(id, options = {}) {
  const root = path.resolve(options.stateDir || process.env.AGENTLOOP_STATE_DIR || path.join(__dirname, '../state'));
  const evidence = [], errors = [];
  function capture(file, optional = false) {
    try {
      const raw = fs.readFileSync(file, 'utf8');
      evidence.push({ file, raw });
      return raw;
    } catch (error) {
      if (!(optional && error.code === 'ENOENT')) errors.push({ file, message: error.message });
      return null;
    }
  }
  function json(file, optional = false) {
    const raw = capture(file, optional);
    if (raw === null) return null;
    try { return JSON.parse(raw); }
    catch (error) { errors.push({ file, message: error.message }); return null; }
  }
  function entries(dir) {
    try { return fs.readdirSync(dir).sort(); }
    catch (error) { if (error.code !== 'ENOENT') errors.push({ file: dir, message: error.message }); return []; }
  }
  const db = json(path.join(root, 'milestone-grants.json'));
  if (db?.version !== 1 || !Object.hasOwn(db.grants || {}, id)) throw new Error('Unknown grant or invalid grant store; preserve and reconcile the store.');
  const grant = db.grants[id];
  const projects = json(options.projectsPath || process.env.AGENTLOOP_PROJECTS_PATH || path.join(__dirname, '../autopilot-projects.json'));
  const project = projects?.[grant.project];
  const jobs = [];
  if (project) {
    const dir = resolveStateDir(grant.project, project, root);
    for (const file of entries(dir).filter(name => /^issue-[1-9]\d*\.json$/.test(name))) {
      const job = json(path.join(dir, file));
      if (job?.repo === grant.repo && job.project === grant.project) jobs.push(job);
    }
    for (const file of entries(dir).filter(name => /^issue-[1-9]\d*\.execution\.ndjson$/.test(name))) capture(path.join(dir, file));
  } else errors.push({ message: 'Project registration missing; restore the owner registration before execution.' });
  // Queue records and their complete journals survive a new operator conversation.
  const queueTasks = [];
  for (const stage of ['pending', 'running', 'done']) {

      const task = json(path.join(root, 'tasks', stage, file));
      if (task?.project === grant.project) {

        capture(path.join(root, 'results', task.id + '.json'), true);
        const runId = require('node:crypto').createHash('sha256').update(task.id).digest('hex');
        capture(path.join(root, 'task-runs', runId + '.json'), true);

    }
  }
  // Includes operator command output/errors, even when no receipt was issued.
  for (const file of entries(path.join(root, 'logs')).filter(name => name.startsWith('onboarding-') && name.endsWith('.ndjson'))) capture(path.join(root, 'logs', file));
  capture(path.join(root, 'events.ndjson'), true);

  let now = Date.now();

    if (!/^\d+$/.test(line) || !Number.isSafeInteger(Number(line))) errors.push({ message: 'Invalid durable authorization clock; reconcile before execution.' });
    else now = Math.max(now, Number(line));
  }
  const expired = Date.parse(grant.expiresAt) <= now;
  const state = expired && ['active', 'draft', 'paused'].includes(grant.state) ? 'expired' : grant.state;
  const receipts = Object.values(grant.receipts || {});

findings.summary:
1) The durable handoff points to evidence files that are not in this PR. docs/issue-111-handoff.md links evidence/issue-111/npm-test-sandbox.log, evidence/issue-111/npm-test.log (the 723-test full run) and evidence/issue-111/batch-tests.log (the 15 test results). The diff adds only implementation.sha256, rehearsal-acceptance.json and rehearsal.json.gz under docs/evidence/issue-111/. These three logs are the only retained record of the full-suite and sandbox-failure results the handoff cites, so the links are dead and the report of remaining limits is unverifiable. Commit the three logs, or remove the claims and links and state where the output is kept. The retained output must be complete and unmodified, per ADR 0001.

2) The handoff's delivery status is stale for the delivered head. It says the implementation 'remains a working-tree change', that the exact-head review and remote CI are still outstanding, and that gh auth is invalid so CI verification is blocked. The PR head 9661ba4 is committed and has a green CI run (#39893058022). Update the handoff to name the delivered SHA and its CI run. Say plainly that independent review is still performed by the guarded pipeline rather than by the local failed Claude attempts. Also state that implementation.sha256 was computed over the tested contents and re-check that it still matches src/milestone-summary.js, src/cli.js and test/milestone-batches.test.js at this head.

3) Minor: the out-of-scope ready-labeled #202 is reported as 'waiting', with the reason 'No receipt; publish and obtain exact owner scope approval'. The lastAdmission decision is NEEDS_APPROVAL and the issue was never in the grant, so an owner reading the summary could take it as pending work. Mark or explain it as a non-grant issue that was blocked (denied) so the 'denied' state in the acceptance criteria is actually shown. Add a test assertion on that status.

findings.summary:
1) The durable handoff points to evidence files that are not in this PR. docs/issue-111-handoff.md links evidence/issue-111/npm-test-sandbox.log, evidence/issue-111/npm-test.log (the 723-test full run) and evidence/issue-111/batch-tests.log (the 15 test results). The diff adds only implementation.sha256, rehearsal-acceptance.json and rehearsal.json.gz under docs/evidence/issue-111/. These three logs are the only retained record of the full-suite and sandbox-failure results the handoff cites, so the links are dead and the report of remaining limits is unverifiable. Commit the three logs, or remove the claims and links and state where the output is kept. The retained output must be complete and unmodified, per ADR 0001.

2) The handoff's delivery status is stale for the delivered head. It says the implementation 'remains a working-tree change', that the exact-head review and remote CI are still outstanding, and that gh auth is invalid so CI verification is blocked. The PR head 9661ba4 is committed and has a green CI run (#39893058022). Update the handoff to name the delivered SHA and its CI run. Say plainly that independent review is still performed by the guarded pipeline rather than by the local failed Claude attempts. Also state that implementation.sha256 was computed over the tested contents and re-check that it still matches src/milestone-summary.js, src/cli.js and test/milestone-batches.test.js at this head.

3) Minor: the out-of-scope ready-labeled #202 is reported as 'waiting', with the reason 'No receipt; publish and obtain exact owner scope approval'. The lastAdmission decision is NEEDS_APPROVAL and the issue was never in the grant, so an owner reading the summary could take it as pending work. Mark or explain it as a non-grant issue that was blocked (denied) so the 'denied' state in the acceptance criteria is actually shown. Add a test assertion on that status.

findings.summary:
1) The durable handoff points to evidence files that are not in this PR. docs/issue-111-handoff.md links evidence/issue-111/npm-test-sandbox.log, evidence/issue-111/npm-test.log (the 723-test full run) and evidence/issue-111/batch-tests.log (the 15 test results). The diff adds only implementation.sha256, rehearsal-acceptance.json and rehearsal.json.gz under docs/evidence/issue-111/. These three logs are the only retained record of the full-suite and sandbox-failure results the handoff cites, so the links are dead and the report of remaining limits is unverifiable. Commit the three logs, or remove the claims and links and state where the output is kept. The retained output must be complete and unmodified, per ADR 0001.

2) The handoff's delivery status is stale for the delivered head. It says the implementation 'remains a working-tree change', that the exact-head review and remote CI are still outstanding, and that gh auth is invalid so CI verification is blocked. The PR head 9661ba4 is committed and has a green CI run (#39893058022). Update the handoff to name the delivered SHA and its CI run. Say plainly that independent review is still performed by the guarded pipeline rather than by the local failed Claude attempts. Also state that implementation.sha256 was computed over the tested contents and re-check that it still matches src/milestone-summary.js, src/cli.js and test/milestone-batches.test.js at this head.

3) Minor: the out-of-scope ready-labeled #202 is reported as 'waiting', with the reason 'No receipt; publish and obtain exact owner scope approval'. The lastAdmission decision is NEEDS_APPROVAL and the issue was never in the grant, so an owner reading the summary could take it as pending work. Mark or explain it as a non-grant issue that was blocked (denied) so the 'denied' state in the acceptance criteria is actually shown. Add a test assertion on that status.

findings.summary:
1) The durable handoff points to evidence files that are not in this PR. docs/issue-111-handoff.md links evidence/issue-111/npm-test-sandbox.log, evidence/issue-111/npm-test.log (the 723-test full run) and evidence/issue-111/batch-tests.log (the 15 test results). The diff adds only implementation.sha256, rehearsal-acceptance.json and rehearsal.json.gz under docs/evidence/issue-111/. These three logs are the only retained record of the full-suite and sandbox-failure results the handoff cites, so the links are dead and the report of remaining limits is unverifiable. Commit the three logs, or remove the claims and links and state where the output is kept. The retained output must be complete and unmodified, per ADR 0001.

2) The handoff's delivery status is stale for the delivered head. It says the implementation 'remains a working-tree change', that the exact-head review and remote CI are still outstanding, and that gh auth is invalid so CI verification is blocked. The PR head 9661ba4 is committed and has a green CI run (#39893058022). Update the handoff to name the delivered SHA and its CI run. Say plainly that independent review is still performed by the guarded pipeline rather than by the local failed Claude attempts. Also state that implementation.sha256 was computed over the tested contents and re-check that it still matches src/milestone-summary.js, src/cli.js and test/milestone-batches.test.js at this head.

3) Minor: the out-of-scope ready-labeled #202 is reported as 'waiting', with the reason 'No receipt; publish and obtain exact owner scope approval'. The lastAdmission decision is NEEDS_APPROVAL and the issue was never in the grant, so an owner reading the summary could take it as pending work. Mark or explain it as a non-grant issue that was blocked (denied) so the 'denied' state in the acceptance criteria is actually shown. Add a test assertion on that status.

findings.summary:
1) The durable handoff points to evidence files that are not in this PR. docs/issue-111-handoff.md links evidence/issue-111/npm-test-sandbox.log, evidence/issue-111/npm-test.log (the 723-test full run) and evidence/issue-111/batch-tests.log (the 15 test results). The diff adds only implementation.sha256, rehearsal-acceptance.json and rehearsal.json.gz under docs/evidence/issue-111/. These three logs are the only retained record of the full-suite and sandbox-failure results the handoff cites, so the links are dead and the report of remaining limits is unverifiable. Commit the three logs, or remove the claims and links and state where the output is kept. The retained output must be complete and unmodified, per ADR 0001.

2) The handoff's delivery status is stale for the delivered head. It says the implementation 'remains a working-tree change', that the exact-head review and remote CI are still outstanding, and that gh auth is invalid so CI verification is blocked. The PR head 9661ba4 is committed and has a green CI run (#39893058022). Update the handoff to name the delivered SHA and its CI run. Say plainly that independent review is still performed by the guarded pipeline rather than by the local failed Claude attempts. Also state that implementation.sha256 was computed over the tested contents and re-check that it still matches src/milestone-summary.js, src/cli.js and test/milestone-batches.test.js at this head.

3) Minor: the out-of-scope ready-labeled #202 is reported as 'waiting', with the reason 'No receipt; publish and obtain exact owner scope approval'. The lastAdmission decision is NEEDS_APPROVAL and the issue was never in the grant, so an owner reading the summary could take it as pending work. Mark or explain it as a non-grant issue that was blocked (denied) so the 'denied' state in the acceptance criteria is actually shown. Add a test assertion on that status.

findings.summary:
1) The durable handoff points to evidence files that are not in this PR. docs/issue-111-handoff.md links evidence/issue-111/npm-test-sandbox.log, evidence/issue-111/npm-test.log (the 723-test full run) and evidence/issue-111/batch-tests.log (the 15 test results). The diff adds only implementation.sha256, rehearsal-acceptance.json and rehearsal.json.gz under docs/evidence/issue-111/. These three logs are the only retained record of the full-suite and sandbox-failure results the handoff cites, so the links are dead and the report of remaining limits is unverifiable. Commit the three logs, or remove the claims and links and state where the output is kept. The retained output must be complete and unmodified, per ADR 0001.

2) The handoff's delivery status is stale for the delivered head. It says the implementation 'remains a working-tree change', that the exact-head review and remote CI are still outstanding, and that gh auth is invalid so CI verification is blocked. The PR head 9661ba4 is committed and has a green CI run (#39893058022). Update the handoff to name the delivered SHA and its CI run. Say plainly that independent review is still performed by the guarded pipeline rather than by the local failed Claude attempts. Also state that implementation.sha256 was computed over the tested contents and re-check that it still matches src/milestone-summary.js, src/cli.js and test/milestone-batches.test.js at this head.

3) Minor: the out-of-scope ready-labeled #202 is reported as 'waiting', with the reason 'No receipt; publish and obtain exact owner scope approval'. The lastAdmission decision is NEEDS_APPROVAL and the issue was never in the grant, so an owner reading the summary could take it as pending work. Mark or explain it as a non-grant issue that was blocked (denied) so the 'denied' state in the acceptance criteria is actually shown. Add a test assertion on that status.
